claims.claim: A Chorus prologue about two feuding households in Verona
claims.evidence: 'Two households, both alike in dignity, In fair Verona'

claims.claim: Act I opens in a public place with armed Capulet servants Sampson and Gregory
claims.evidence: 'SCENE I. A public place. Enter Sampson and Gregory armed with swords and bucklers'; Dramatis Personae: servants to Capulet

claims.claim: They pick a quarrel with Montague servants; brawl spreads until the Prince stops it
claims.evidence: 'Draw thy tool; here comes of the house of Montagues'; 'Enter Prince Escalus'

claims.claim: Romeo, a Montague, sneaks into the Capulets' feast and falls in love with Juliet
claims.evidence: masks, 'ancient feast of Capulet's'; Romeo and Juliet meet; text does not say 'sneaks'
claims.fix: Romeo, a Montague, goes masked to the Capulets' feast and falls in love with Juliet.

claims.claim: Friar Lawrence secretly marries them
claims.evidence: Friar Lawrence's cell scenes (II.vi)

claims.claim: Tybalt kills Mercutio, Romeo kills Tybalt, Prince banishes Romeo to Mantua
claims.evidence: 'Mercutio slain'; 'Tybalt slain'; 'Romeo banished'; 'Welcome from Mantua'

claims.claim: Capulet plans to marry Juliet to Paris
claims.evidence: 'Enter Capulet, Paris'; Paris 'a young Nobleman'

claims.claim: The Friar gives her a potion to feign death
claims.evidence: Friar Lawrence's plan; Juliet 'dies' and is placed in the tomb

claims.claim: His letter to Romeo goes astray
claims.evidence: Friar John: 'I could not send it,—here it is again'

claims.claim: Hearing she is dead, Romeo buys poison
claims.evidence: Apothecary scene; 'Poison hath residence'

claims.claim: Romeo kills Paris and himself in the Capulet tomb
claims.evidence: Paris: 'O, I am slain!'; Romeo '[Dies.]'; 'A churchyard; in it a Monument belonging to the Capulets'

claims.claim: Juliet wakes and stabs herself
claims.evidence: 'O happy dagger... [stabs herself]'

claims.claim: Their deaths end the feud
claims.evidence: 'O brother Montague, give me thy hand'; 'Poor sacrifices of our enmity'

claims.claim: Juliet's Nurse carries their messages
claims.evidence: Nurse to Juliet, go-between scenes

claims.claim: Friar John, sent with the letter, is delayed
claims.evidence: searchers 'Seal'd up the doors'; 'my speed to Mantua there was stay'd'

claims.claim: Romeo: son of Montague
claims.evidence: 'ROMEO, son to Montague'

claims.claim: Juliet: Capulet's daughter, not yet fourteen
claims.evidence: 'JULIET, daughter to Capulet'; 'She's not fourteen'

claims.claim: Friar Lawrence marries them and plans the potion
claims.evidence: text

claims.claim: Mercutio: Romeo's friend, kinsman to the Prince
claims.evidence: 'MERCUTIO, kinsman to the Prince, and friend to Romeo'

claims.claim: Tybalt: Juliet's hot-tempered cousin
claims.evidence: 'Tybalt, my cousin! O my brother's child!' (Lady Capulet)

claims.claim: Nurse: Juliet's go-between
claims.evidence: 'NURSE to Juliet'

claims.claim: Paris: nobleman Capulet wants Juliet to marry
claims.evidence: 'PARIS, a young Nobleman'
